name: CO-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+29 partisan lean makes this Denver-based seat nearly unwinnable for Republicans
Kiros has raised $1.1M to Peterson's roughly $2K, an overwhelming financial edge
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97%
Open seat after DeGette's retirement is the only nominal source of uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's D+29 lean, Kiros's roughly five-hundred-to-one fundraising advantage, and market pricing near 97% leave no plausible path for Peterson; the open seat barely moves the needle in a seat this partisan.
model.watch: Only an extraordinary unforeseen development, such as a major scandal or an unusual third-party surge, would put the Republican within striking distance.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Diana DeGette (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Colorado's 1st District, centered on Denver, carries a partisan lean of D+29, making it one of the most Democratic House seats in the country. Diana DeGette's retirement creates an open seat, but the district's fundamentals remain overwhelmingly favorable to the party that has held it. Democrat Melat Kiros enters the general election with a large war chest, while Republican Christy Peterson has raised only about two thousand dollars.

Kiros has drawn substantial outside spending, much of it tied to a contested primary, and prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97 percent. No general-election polls are available, but with fundamentals this lopsided the race is rated Safe Democratic, with the open-seat transition the only nominal source of uncertainty.
